chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Udhaynah, who said:
I wrote to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) asking him about a man who had wood, so he sold it to those who make flutes from it. He said: 'There is no problem.'
And (I asked him) about a man who had wood, so he sold it to the one who takes it to make crosses from it. He said: 'No.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to sell wood to Christians for making crosses?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* illustrates the Shia juristic principle of *al-istishab* and contextual permissibility (*al-ibaha al-idafi*), where the ruling on an object depends on its primary end-use rather than its intrinsic nature. It highlights the distinction between *barabit* (likely referring to reed flutes or similar instruments) and *sultan* (crosses), reflecting the early Imams' nuanced approach to cultural artifacts used in worship or daily life. This ruling underscores the Shia view that items used for permissible purposes remain pure and tradable, even if used by others for different ends, provided the seller is not directly facilitating idolatry.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Azina who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> asking him<sup>asws</sup> about a man from whom were planks of wood, so he sold it to the ones who make flutes from it. So he<sup>asws</sup> said; ‘There is not problem’.
And (I asked him<sup>asws</sup>) about a man who had some wood for him, so he sold it to the one who takes it make crosses out of it’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Udhaynah who has said the following: “I once wrote to abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked about a man who had a piece of wood and sold it to those who make barbat (musical tool) out of it. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful.’
